nodes.label: FluxIPC — Namespace-tree IPC library for Linux (CLAUDE.md)
nodes.norm_label: fluxipc — namespace-tree ipc library for linux (claude.md)

nodes.label: Six-Layer Bottom-Up Component Architecture
nodes.rationale: FluxIPC is organized into 6 layers bottom-up: namespace tree (fluxipc_tree.c), shared memory registry (fluxipc_shm.c), socket transport (fluxipc_sock.c), symlink discovery (fluxipc_symlink.c), MCP server (fluxipc_mcp.c), and interactive shell (fluxipc_interactive.c). Each layer builds on the one below it.

nodes.label: Server Lifecycle Flow (client_dispatch → server_init → register → poll → destroy)
nodes.rationale: The server lifecycle follows a strict sequence: check symlink client dispatch, initialize server (creates socket/SHM/symlinks, registers static entries), optionally register dynamic endpoints, run single select() poll loop, then destroy (stops MCP, removes symlinks, unlinks socket, closes SHM).
nodes.norm_label: server lifecycle flow (client_dispatch → server_init → register → poll → destroy)

nodes.label: Compile-Time Registration via ELF Section (FLUXIPC_STATIC)
nodes.rationale: FLUXIPC_STATIC(path, usage, slot_sz, handler, ctx) places a fluxipc_entry_t into the fluxipc_registry ELF section. At server_init, linker-provided __start_fluxipc_registry / __stop_fluxipc_registry bounds are iterated. Requires -rdynamic so the linker retains section symbols.

nodes.label: Zero External Dependencies Design Principle
nodes.rationale: The MCP server hand-rolls HTTP + JSON parsing with zero external dependencies. The only link-time dependencies are libpthread, librt, and libreadline. This keeps the library lightweight and embeddable.

nodes.label: Single-Threaded select() Event Loop
nodes.rationale: The server uses a single-threaded select() loop that dispatches both IPC socket connections and MCP HTTP connections. Tree operations are mutex-protected for safety but the intended use is one-thread polling.

nodes.label: FluxIPC CSDN Article — Lightweight Linux IPC Framework
nodes.norm_label: fluxipc csdn article — lightweight linux ipc framework

nodes.label: Four Core Design Principles of FluxIPC
nodes.rationale: 1) Namespace tree — IPC endpoints organized as UNIX file paths; 2) Shared memory registry — POSIX shared memory exposes endpoint info for auto-discovery; 3) Zero-config calling — symlinks encode server identity and path; 4) Native MCP support — built-in HTTP MCP server exposes all endpoints as AI-callable tools.
nodes.norm_label: four core design principles of fluxipc

nodes.label: Compile-time + Runtime Dual Registration Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Fixed system interfaces register at compile-time via FLUXIPC_STATIC macro writing to ELF section; hardware-dependent interfaces register at runtime via fluxipc_register() API. Suitable for embedded scenarios where static and dynamic endpoints coexist.

nodes.label: Symlink-Based Zero-Config Client Invocation
nodes.rationale: Each registered endpoint gets a symlink under /run/<prog>-fluxipc/<path> pointing to the executable. When invoked via symlink, argv[0] encodes both server identity and IPC path, enabling zero-configuration client calls without hardcoded server addresses.

nodes.label: Namespace Tree as File System Metaphor
nodes.rationale: IPC endpoints are organized in a hierarchical path structure like a filesystem. Internal nodes are containers; only leaf nodes carry handler functions. Removing a leaf auto-prunes empty ancestors. This makes IPC interfaces as intuitive as navigating a file system.
nodes.norm_label: namespace tree as file system metaphor

nodes.label: Built-in MCP Server for AI Agent Integration
nodes.rationale: FluxIPC embeds an MCP (Model Context Protocol) HTTP server that auto-exposes all registered IPC endpoints as MCP tools. Claude Desktop, Cursor, Windsurf, and other AI clients can discover and call IPC interfaces through natural language. Slashes in paths become underscores in tool names.
nodes.norm_label: built-in mcp server for ai agent integration

nodes.label: Interactive Shell with Tab Completion and Range Syntax
nodes.rationale: Readline-based REPL with tab completion loaded from shared memory, ls/cd/help/watch/reload commands, inline range syntax (start:end:step) for Cartesian-product parameter sweeps, and ! prefix to execute system commands without leaving the shell.
nodes.norm_label: interactive shell with tab completion and range syntax

nodes.label: Five Client Call Methods (CSDN)
nodes.rationale: FluxIPC supports five ways to invoke IPC endpoints: CLI direct call, symlink invocation, interactive shell, HTTP/MCP (for AI agents), and Python client. Each method targets different use cases from shell scripting to AI integration.

nodes.label: IPC Solutions Comparison (FluxIPC vs D-Bus vs gRPC vs Raw Unix Socket)
nodes.rationale: FluxIPC compares favorably on: interface definition simplicity (path strings vs XML/Protobuf), service discovery (shared memory auto-discovery vs daemon/manual), CLI debugging (built-in interactive shell vs dbus-send/netcat), AI Agent integration (built-in MCP vs requiring extra development), and dependency weight (libreadline only vs libdbus+daemon or gRPC toolchain).
nodes.norm_label: ipc solutions comparison (fluxipc vs d-bus vs grpc vs raw unix socket)

nodes.norm_label: fluxipc — lightweight namespace-tree ipc library for linux (readme)

nodes.label: Design Notes — No Daemon, Symlink Resolution, Hand-rolled MCP
nodes.rationale: Key design decisions: namespace tree with internal container nodes and leaf handlers; process-shared pthread_rwlock_t in SHM for safe concurrent reads; symlink argv[0] encodes server identity and IPC path; no external daemon — server embeds IPC as library; MCP server hand-rolls HTTP+JSON with zero external deps, supports Streamable HTTP (2025-03-26) and legacy SSE (2024-11-05).
